summary: Round 2. All three round-1 findings are fixed in the code, and I found no regressions. CLEANUP-001 is resolved. validate_failure (qualify_cleanup.py:42-50) now requires the error to equal repr(InterruptedError('adapter received signal N')) exactly. N is the injected signal for the SIG cases and signal.SIGTERM for controller-timeout. That matches the adapter's handler text (perlmutter_adapter.py:103) and failure.json's repr(error) (perlmutter_adapter.py:146). The step-timeout case must start with 'TimeoutExpired(' and fall in the 60-70 s window. Offline tests show SIGHUP rejects 'signal 15' and controller-timeout rejects a SIGHUP receipt. CLEANUP-002 is resolved. The finally block saves sys.exc_info()[1], which holds the in-flight exception on the exception path, into harness-cleanup.json. failed.json now also records error.__context__, so the original cause is kept when 'harness cleanup uncertain' replaces it. CLEANUP-003 is resolved. The acceptance check is now a pure function, with rejection tests for wrong signal, wrong type, unrelated cancelled step, uncertain cleanup and both timeout-window edges. The new qualify.sbatch is bounded and consistent with CLEANUP.md and scope.md: 15 minutes, premium lcls_g, 1 node, 4x16 CPUs, 1 GPU, disable-binding, an EXIT sacct trap, a frozen-source checksum check, pinned Python, a pinned runtime hash and a fresh per-job output path. There are no blocking findings. Two optional, low-severity items remain. This approves the harness only as fit for bounded fault injection before hardware. It makes no hardware or qualification claim.
checks: Read scope.md, validation-01.md, context-01.md, review-01.json, response-01.md, status.json and qualify.sbatch at df42d1cd6.

CLEANUP-001 resolved: qualify_cleanup.py:49-50 uses an exact repr equality. For SIGHUP the only accepted string is 'adapter received signal 1', so 'signal 15' is rejected (test_qualify_cleanup.py:32). For controller-timeout the expected signal is SIGTERM, which matches campaign.run_command's os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGTERM) on TimeoutExpired (campaign.py:229-232). The adapter is the session leader there because of start_new_session=True. Step-timeout requires the prefix 'TimeoutExpired(' plus 60 <= seconds < 70 (lines 46-47), and both edges are tested (test lines 45-48).

CLEANUP-002 resolved: at qualify_cleanup.py:143 sys.exc_info() inside finally returns the propagating exception on the exceptional path (Python 3 pushes exc_info for finally handlers), and on the normal path it is None because run_case is called from a try body, not an except. harness-cleanup.json records original_error (line 157). failed.json records __context__ (line 192), which Python sets automatically when require() raises inside finally.

CLEANUP-003 resolved: validate_failure is pure and covered by test_failure_receipt_rejects_wrong_signal_and_cleanup and test_timeout_receipt_rejects_wrong_cause_and_grace. There are 5 tests in total, matching the reported '5 harness rejection tests PASS'.

No regressions in run_case: readiness 25 s / 20 s, exact identity(), distinct target and sentinel IDs, both live under exact names before injection, the adapter PID equals the Popen PID for the SIG cases, exit-code expectations (1 for adapter, 0 for controller), signal cleanup < 10 s, controller < 70 s, no scheduler.json/complete.json, target gone, sentinel still present with the same ID, two post-cleanup heartbeat advances, graceful release exit 0, then confirm_step COMPLETED/0:0. All of these are unchanged from round 1.

Bounded cleanup is unchanged: cancel_step has a 6 s total budget, the finally block cancels only the two unique names with 10 s + 2 s process waits, and cleanup_worker has a 240 s self-deadline. The sum of the case bounds is well under the 15-minute sbatch limit.

qualify.sbatch matches the documented resource request and CLEANUP.md. The trap is installed before module load and checksum setup, PYTHONPATH/PYTHONHOME/LD_PRELOAD are unset, MPICH_GPU_SUPPORT_ENABLED=0, the script runs from the frozen-01 copy, and it passes the pinned runtime JSON and SHA. It requests no dataset access and sets no qualification flags.
Shared adapter launch/cancel_step/confirm_step and campaign.run_command were inspected and are unchanged in behaviour relevant to this harness.
limitations: I only read files; I did not run any tests. The 5 harness, 30 adapter and 20 controller PASS results are as reported by the coordinator (status.json and the review prompt). They are not in a committed validation note.

No hardware run evidence or raw scratch was available; this is a pre-hardware code review. Slurm behaviour (squeue/sacct lag, how --overlap/--exact interacts with the target's --exclusive, srun's forwarding of SIGTERM in the controller case) is judged from the code only.

The frozen-01 directory, its SHA256SUMS and runtime-01.json are scratch artifacts outside the repository and were not inspected. Whether the frozen copy matches df42d1cd6 can only be confirmed from the hardware evidence.
The ruling that the Python finally-block sys.exc_info() captures the in-flight exception comes from language semantics, not from running the code.

The round-2 results (5 harness, 30 adapter, 20 controller PASS) appear only in status.json 'checks' and the coordinator's prompt. There is no committed validation record tied to df42d1cd6.

findings.evidence: Tests check positive acceptance only for SIGHUP and step-timeout. The controller-timeout case accepting repr(InterruptedError('adapter received signal 15')) and the SIGTERM/SIGINT positive receipts are not exercised offline. They follow from the same expression at qualify_cleanup.py:49-50, so the risk is minimal.
findings.requested_change: Optional: add a loop that sets each case label to its expected signal number and asserts validate_failure accepts the matching receipt. Include controller-timeout -> 15 so a future change to the label-to-signal mapping is caught offline.
